summary: Provision ephemeral Slack channel lifecycle automation with Confluence page auto-linking and enforced metadata tags
description:
Issue summary:
Request: create an automated provisioning workflow that produces timebound Slack channels for short-lived initiatives (workshops, incident triage, external partner reviews) and automatically links/creates a Confluence seed page with enforced metadata tags.

Impact:
- Reduces manual steps when creating ephemeral channels and associated docs.
- Ensures consistent channel-to-doc traceability for audits and incident reviews.
- Prevents orphaned channels by enforcing lifecycle archival and metadata capture.

Request details / scope:
- A Slack-bot-driven self-service flow (slash command or form) to create an ephemeral channel with a TTL (default 30 days, configurable).
- On creation, automatically create a Confluence page seeded from a template and insert the Confluence link as the channel header/pinned post.
- Apply a set of required metadata tags to the Confluence page (project, data-classification, owner, retention-policy). Bot should fail and return guidance if required metadata is missing.
- Attach a lifecycle automation that: 1) posts reminders at configurable intervals pre-archive; 2) archives the channel and snapshots minimal history to Confluence when TTL expires; 3) notifies channel owners and the platform-pod before final archive.
- RBAC: only members of specific groups can create external-facing ephemeral channels; all creations must be recorded to an audit log (accessible to security).

Acceptance criteria:
- Self-service flow creates Slack channel + Confluence page and adds a pinned link in channel within 60s of request.
- Mandatory metadata enforcement prevents page creation unless required fields are provided.
- Channel archival workflow triggers reminders at 7 days and 1 day before archive and archives automatically at TTL expiry.
- Audit record for each creation and archive event is persisted to the central audit feed.
- Documentation page and runbook created in Confluence with sample template and troubleshooting steps.

Security considerations:
- Bot authentication must use service account scoped narrowly for channel creation and Confluence page creation only.
- Ensure pages seeded for external partner channels default to "restricted" view and follow retention settings.

Rollout plan and phasing:
1) PoC in staging with platform-pod and one pilot team (Developer Experience) for two weeks.
2) Security review and small fixes.
3) Gradual enablement for all pods with opt-in flag.

Notes:
- Prefer reusable automation code already in github.com/redwood/automation-scripts to avoid duplicate maintenance.
- Keep onboarding UX simple (slash command + modal).
steps_to_reproduce: N/A — this is a provisioning/automation request rather than a defect. Example desired flow: 1) /ephemeral create --name onboarding-workshop --ttl 14 --partner-external true 2) Modal prompts for metadata 3) On submit, channel created, Confluence page created, pinned link posted, and audit logged.
